records.people: Taron Jackman (Director, board of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority; Partner at Deloitte in the Cayman Islands from 2004 until his retirement from Deloitte in 2025)
records.move: from the Audit Department of Price Waterhouse in the Cayman Islands, then ten years at Barclays Bank & Trust (Cayman) Limited rising to Chief Operating Officer, then Partner at Deloitte from 2004 until retirement from Deloitte in 2025, to Director on the board of the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority
records.summary: The private side is the employer side: CIMA's own biography of its director Taron Jackman states he was a Partner of the Deloitte Cayman firm from 2004 until retiring in 2025 and before that spent ten years at Barclays Bank & Trust (Cayman) Limited, reaching Chief Operating Officer. Deloitte is a privately held professional-services partnership network - the page's own words are 'the Caribbean and Bermuda Deloitte Member firm' and 'the Deloitte firms in Barbados and Trinidad and Tobago' - and its Cayman practice sells audit, regulatory and risk advisory work to the financial-services industry, which is the financial leg. The page does not use the word private and makes no ownership statement about Barclays Bank & Trust (Cayman) Limited either, calling it only 'a Class A Registered Bank in the Cayman Islands'; that bank is therefore NOT the basis of this record, and the private finding rests on the Deloitte partnership alone. The page gives no date for his appointment to the CIMA board; CIMA's board page (https://www.cima.ky/the-board, read 17 November 2026) lists him as a serving Director, which is the second source for the central-bank side. The 2004 and 2025 dates are both printed on the cited page. Distinct from the one record the map already holds for the Cayman Islands (Greg Swart, Farallon Capital Management LLC).
records.source_title: Cayman Islands Monetary Authority - Taron Jackman, Director (board biography)

records.people: Øystein Børsum (Deputy Governor of Norges Bank, appointed for the period 2 August 2021-2027; Second Deputy Chair of the Executive Board and of the Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Committee)
records.move: from chief economist at Swedbank to Deputy Governor of Norges Bank, with particular responsibility for the Government Pension Fund Global
records.summary: Norges Bank's own Executive Board page states that Øystein Børsum was 'Appointed Deputy Governor for the period 2 August 2021-2027' and that 'His work experience includes the post of chief economist at Swedbank and positions in the Budget and Asset Management Departments of the Ministry of Finance'. The private side is the prior employer, Swedbank: the bank is listed in its own right, not a subsidiary and not state-owned, and the evidence is Swedbank's own investor-relations page for its share, which states 'Swedbank's A shares are listed on NASDAQ OMX Stockholm in the Large Cap segment' (second source: https://www.swedbank.com/investor-relations/the-share.html, read 17 November 2026). What is unsettled is the holder side: Swedbank's shareholders page says its largest shareholders are published monthly from Euroclear data but the table itself is behind a cookie gate and was not read, so no individual holder is named here. Norges Bank's page gives no years for the Swedbank post; the only dates in this record are the appointment dates printed on it. Distinct from the one record the map holds for Norway (Nicolai Tangen, AKO Capital to Norges Bank Investment Management).
records.source_title: Norges Bank - The Executive Board (members' biographies)

records.people: Ulrik Nødgaard (Governor of Danmarks Nationalbank since 15 August 2024; CEO of Finance Denmark 2015-2024; Director General of the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority 2009-2015)
records.move: from chief executive of Finance Denmark, the financial sector's own business and employers' organisation, to Governor of Danmarks Nationalbank
records.summary: Danmarks Nationalbank's own biography page states 'Governor since 15 August 2024' and lists under previous positions 'CEO of Finance Denmark 2015-2024', 'Director General of the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority 2009-2015', and under boards 'Member of the Board of Directors, Chairman of Audit Committee PKA 2017-2024'. The private side is Finance Denmark, which is not a state body but the industry's own body: its own About us page says 'Finance Denmark is the business and employers' organisation for the financial sector. We represent banks, mortgage institutions, asset management, securities trading and investment funds' (second source: https://finansdanmark.dk/en/about-us/, read 17 November 2026). That is the financial leg - a private membership and employers' organisation financed by its member banks, not a company with shareholders, so no ownership percentage exists to quote; the evidence is its own description of itself and its membership. His other legs are public (the Danish FSA and the Ministry of Economic and Business Affairs). All years here are printed on the cited page. Distinct from the one record the map holds for Denmark (Lars Rohde, Realkredit Danmark and ATP to the Board of Governors and afterwards Nordea).
records.source_title: Danmarks Nationalbank - Ulrik Nødgaard, Governor (official biography)

blanks.note: NOT IN MY ASSIGNMENT (Pakistan already holds two counted records) but it was the named lead, so it was tested and closed. Vein closed on two of the four named deputy-governor pages. sbp.org.pk/about/governors/DG5.htm read in full through the fetch tool: it is Jameel Ahmad, and the only employers it names are the State Bank of Pakistan (from 1991) and the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) as Advisor July 2009 to April 2015 - two central banks, no private employer, no ownership wording. sbp.org.pk/about/governors/DG9.htm read in full: it is Dr Inayat Hussain, appointed Deputy Governor on 10 November 2021 for three years; the page carries no career history at all, naming no prior employer and no dates before the SBP role, only 'diversified experience spanned over two decades in banking supervision'. DG10 and DG11 were NOT REACHED - budget went to target countries instead.

Confirmed blank on this route. Bank of Jamaica's own corporate-governance index (boj.org.jm/?p=199) and its Board of Directors page (https://boj.org.jm/about-boj/board-of-directors/) were both read in full on 17 November 2026. The board page is a bare list of seven names - Brian Langrin (Governor and Chairman), Wayne Robinson, E. George Roper, Christine Clarke, Andrea Coy, Richard Powell, Serge Trevor Alleyne - with no biographies, no employers and no appointment dates. There is nothing on the bank's own site to build a career move from; a second Jamaican record would have to come from the appointed directors' own employers' filings or from BOJ press releases per director, which were not opened.

Refused, and a close one worth recording. The Central Bank of Trinidad and Tobago's leadership page (https://www.central-bank.org.tt/?p=1349, read 17 November 2026) carries a full dated biography of Governor Larry Howai: appointed 11th Governor on 24 June 2025, Minister of Finance and the Economy 2012-2015, previously Chief Executive Officer of the First Citizens Group, Chairman of the National Gas Company and of the National Energy Corporation, and 'Director on the Board of ANSA McAL Limited from 2016 to 2025'. Every leg the page names is either a state body (First Citizens, NGC, National Energy, the ministry) or a diversified conglomerate whose ownership and whose financial character the page does not state. ANSA McAL Limited is not described as private, not described as financial, and no shareholder is named, so counting it would assert both. The financial leg was not found on this page. Next step for a later round: ANSA McAL's own annual report, which would settle both the ownership and whether his directorship covered its banking and insurance subsidiaries.

Second candidate logged, not filed, alongside the filed Jackman record. Monique Frederick, Director of CIMA, per her CIMA biography (https://www.cima.ky/monique-frederick, read 17 November 2026) 'is the Head of Wealth Management at Butterfield Bank (Cayman) Limited with responsibility for leading the Asset Management and Private Banking departments' - a concurrent private financial seat of exactly the admitted shape - but the page gives NO dates at all (only 'over 25 years of experience in wealth management') and makes no ownership statement about Butterfield Bank (Cayman) Limited. Per the rule that with no years you hold it, it is held. One fetch of Butterfield's own group-structure page plus a CIMA appointment date would convert it. Also read https://www.cima.ky/mr-vaughan-carter: dated (first appointed 2023, reappointed 2025 and 2026) but every role named is public or a law practice, so no private financial leg.

Vein closed on the board page itself, not on Bermuda. The Bermuda Monetary Authority's own Board of Directors page (https://bma.bm/board-of-directors, read 17 November 2026) names twelve directors with their outside posts, including PHILIP BUTTERFIELD, 'Chairman, HSBC Bank of Bermuda (retired)', RON HAMILTON, 'Senior Vice President, Swiss Re', MARK CROCKWELL, 'Treasurer, Saïd Holdings Limited', and TAMMY RICHARDSON-AUGUSTUS, 'Retired Partner, Appleby (Bermuda) Limited'. Two of these are private financial employers on their face, but the page gives NO dates - not one appointment date or term for any director - and makes no ownership statement about any of them. The page does say terms 'normally' run three to five years, which is not a date. Named lead for the next round: the BMA's own annual report, which lists the Board with appointment dates, read together with HSBC's or Swiss Re's own group-structure statement; and the per-director bio PDFs, of which only two are still linked from the page (Michael Leverock and Donald Scott).

Refused, with the document named. Banco de Guatemala's own published list of Junta Monetaria members (https://banguat.gob.gt/sites/default/files/banguat/Publica/leyaccesoalainfo/miembros_jm.pdf, 13 kB, read in full 17 November 2026) names LUIS ROLANDO LARA GROJEC as a titular member 'Electo por los presidentes de los consejos de administración o juntas directivas de los bancos privados nacionales', and ENRIQUE ANTONIO JOSÉ RODRÍGUEZ MAHR as the alternate in the same seat - the word privados is the bank's own. But the document is a bare list: it gives no term dates, no years and, decisively, does not name either man's own employer, so there is no stated employer whose ownership could be checked and no date to anchor a move. A seat elected BY private banks is not by itself a statement that the holder worked for one. Named lead: Banguat's Memoria de Labores 2024, which sets out the Junta Monetaria with the members' terms.

Two further Norwegian candidates logged from the same Executive Board page, both held for want of dates. THOMAS EKELI, external board member 'for the period to 15 May 2028', whose experience includes 'chief economist at the Government Pension Fund Norway and Pareto Securities' - Pareto Securities is a private investment firm but no years are given for it and the page makes no ownership statement. RAGNHILD JANBU FRESVIK, board member to 15 May 2028, with 'work experience from Sparebanken Vest, Borea and Boston Consulting Group' - again no years and no ownership statement. HANS AASNÆS mixes private finance (Storebrand, Nordic Trustee, Vertus Capital) with a state investment company (Investinor) in one undated sentence. All three would need a second dated source.

Not reached. One search was run for National Bank of Serbia vice-governors' biographies and returned only press coverage of parliamentary re-elections and encyclopaedia mirrors, no nbs.rs CV page. The NBS site's own management pages were never opened, so Serbia has not actually been tested on this row.
